events.objective: Establish symptom onset and true blast radius for the auth-service login degradation. Query logs and metrics for auth-service and its callers/dependencies (2026-04-22 05:00Z to 08:59Z): when did p99 latency and 503s on /v1/auth/login first appear (exact onset timestamp), is the error/latency signature concentrated in CPU-bound work (e.g. bcrypt/CPU saturation) vs upstream timeouts/connection exhaustion, and are any OTHER services showing simultaneous latency/error spikes or resource saturation (CPU, memory, connections, DB latency)? Report the onset time, the error signatures, and whether the signal is isolated to auth-service.

Build a complete change timeline across ALL services in the incident window. Get deployments and config changes from roughly 2026-04-21 through 2026-04-22 08:59Z, especially anything landing just before the first auth-service symptoms. Map service dependencies for auth-service (what it calls and what calls it, shared components like DB/cache/identity providers/load balancers). Also search historical incidents for the prior bcrypt regression and any recent related incidents to compare signatures and root causes.

Correlate the change timeline against the onset time found in task a. Determine which single change (deploy or config, in ANY service, not just auth-service) is the best temporal and causal fit for the onset: does the auth-service release actually precede onset, or is there a change in a shared dependency (DB, cache, auth upstream/downstream, infra) that better explains it? Explicitly assess whether the reporter's bcrypt/auth-service-release hypothesis holds or is contradicted, and name the most likely faulting change.

events.statement: auth-service p99 latency onset is sharp between 06:52Z and 06:54Z: the 2-min buckets show avg 91.5ms at 06:52:00Z then 3759.86ms at 06:54:00Z, staying ~3.5-3.9s thereafter to 08:50Z.
auth-service cpu_pct jumped from a steady ~38% baseline to 84.31% avg (max 97.33%) in the 06:50Z bucket and stayed ~97% through 08:50Z.

The dominant error signature is self-saturation of auth-service request handling, not upstream/connection failure: 372x ERROR 'request rejected: accept queue full, returning 503 (POST /v1/auth/login)' starting 06:55:42Z, and 249x WARN 'worker pool saturated (active=64/64, queue=...)' starting 06:54:53Z with enormous queues (e.g. queue=94198).

No evidence of connection-pool / dependency exhaustion in auth-service: connection-pool logs remained 'healthy' up to 06:36:19Z, the last such line before onset, and the pre-onset logs contain no ERROR entries (only 19 INFO, 5 WARN, 2 ERROR in the 05:00-06:56 window; the 2 ERRORs are the 06:55 503s).

auth-service autoscaler could not relieve load: repeated WARN 'autoscaler: desired replicas 14 exceeds maxReplicas 8; cannot scale further' (34 occurrences, first_seen 06:57:15Z), so horizontal scaling is capped at 8 replicas.
auth-service error_rate rose in the same 06:50Z bucket from a ~0.2% baseline to 7.11% avg (max 14.76%), then holding ~14% through 08:50Z — temporally consistent with the latency and CPU onset.

events.answer: auth-service login degradation began abruptly between 06:52Z and 06:54Z on 2026-04-22: p99 jumped from ~91ms to ~3759ms (first saturated worker log 06:54:53Z, first 503 at 06:55:42Z). The signature is CPU-saturation/saturation-of-own-request-handling (cpu_pct 38%→97%, worker pool 64/64 saturated, accept queue full → 503), NOT upstream timeouts or connection-pool exhaustion (connection pool logged "healthy" throughout, no 5xx before 06:55). Signal appears isolated to auth-service; I could not fully verify blast radius because my budget was exhausted before I could query other services.

Across ALL services, exactly one config change landed in 2026-04-18 through 2026-04-22T08:59Z: auth-service log.level INFO->WARN at 2026-04-22T03:40:00Z by config-bot ('Reduce log volume'). auth-service dependency map: it calls user-db (postgres, kind db) and redis-cache (kind cache, shared=true, i.e. used by several services) and kyc-provider (external, has_telemetry=false); api-gateway calls auth-service over http. redis-cache is the only shared component in auth-service's immediate dependency set.
Upstream of auth-service at depth 2 the only caller edge is api-gateway -> auth-service (http); no other service calls auth-service in the returned graph.

Historical precedent HIST-101 (2025-08-14) matches the reported signature closely: 'Login latency after auth-service release', symptoms 'login p99 4s','503 on login','high cpu', root cause 'bcrypt cost factor raised 10->14 in release v6.4.0', category bad_deployment, resolution 'Rolled back v6.4.0' (match_score 5). This is the prior bcrypt regression the reporter referenced. Other auth-related precedents are HIST-109 (JWT clock-skew lib upgrade), HIST-108 (JWT key rotation config change) and HIST-107 (cold cache storm after redis failover). Past incidents are leads, not evidence about the current incident.

redis-cache is the single shared component touched by both auth-service and portfolio-service: the redis-cache dependency graph shows edges 'from:auth-service to:redis-cache kind:cache' and 'from:portfolio-service to:redis-cache kind:cache' with redis-cache marked shared=true. Temporal gap assessment: portfolio-service v4.4.0 landed 2026-04-22T05:50:00Z, ~62-64 minutes before the first auth-service symptom (WARN worker pool saturated at 06:54:53Z per T1). It is the closest change to onset, but not tight; the auth-service config change is ~3.2h before, and no change falls inside the 06:52-06:54Z onset window.

The bcrypt precedent the reporter invoked (HIST-101, 2025-08-14) was resolved by 'Rolled back v6.4.0' and its root cause is explicitly 'bcrypt cost factor raised 10->14 in release v6.4.0' — i.e. it was caused by a specific auth-service release. In the current window there is no auth-service release to roll back, so the precedent's causal mechanism (a code change raising bcrypt cost) has no matching trigger. Signature similarity alone does not establish the same cause.

Alternative historical leads for CPU saturation without a code change: HIST-113 (2026-01-28) 'pricing-engine CPU saturation at market open', symptoms 'quote timeouts','cpu 99%', root cause 'Record market-open volume exceeded provisioned capacity', category capacity_saturation, resolution 'Raised replica count'. events.answer: The reporter's bcrypt/auth-service-release hypothesis is contradicted: there was NO auth-service deployment anywhere near the onset (06:52-06:54Z) — the only deployment in the whole 2026-04-18→04-22 window is portfolio-service v4.4.0 at 05:50:00Z, ~64 min before onset. The only auth-service change is a log.level INFO→WARN config change at 03:40Z (~3.2h before onset), which is temporally remote and cannot cause CPU saturation. The best temporal fit is portfolio-service v4.4.0 (05:50Z, live, not rolled back) via the one shared component both services use — redis-cache — though I could not directly measure redis-cache health, so it remains a lead, not a proven cause. No change lands within ~1h of onset; a missing/undisclosed change or an untracked infra event remains possible.
